display: Filipina nanny in Dubai, five years with the same family in Jumeirah, working toward a cabin crew career.

signals.text: I want to apply for cabin crew before I turn 30 next year, and I've been preparing for years.
I only have Fridays off, so I can't go to weekday open days or weekday-evening classes.
The cabin crew academies I've seen cost about 3,000 dirhams, which I can't pay.
A cabin crew open day is coming up on a weekday in October and I can't go. I'd like to know how to get seen another way.
In mock interviews my answers still sound like a nanny CV. I need help turning five years of childcare into crew language.
I'm learning to swim on Friday mornings. I can do almost two lengths, but I still panic when my feet leave the floor.
I'm working on the reach test: I'm 160cm and need to touch a mark at 212cm. I'd like someone to tell me honestly how it works and what the real standard is.
I've watched hundreds of interview videos but have never practised with someone who works or has worked as crew.
I don't dare ask for a fixed weekday evening off. I'd like to learn how to have that conversation well.
I'm travelling to Cebu on 18 December for my sister's wedding, so I'm short of free time and money until then.
I'm unsure what next year will look like, and I'd like to make a decision about it with a clearer head.
I'm afraid that after five years of dreaming I'll fail, or that I'll be told I'm too old after 30.
My family at home relies on the money I send, and my dad's knees are getting worse. It's hard to plan anything for myself.
I'm often tired. I look after other people all day and have little time or energy for myself.

offers.text: Five years of live-in nanny experience with two children: homework help, meal prep, bedtimes, calm handling of tantrums.
First-aid knowledge and experience supervising children around water.
Fluent Filipino-English, plus basic Arabic phrases from daily life in Dubai.
I know the standard cabin crew interview questions by heart. I can be a mock-interview partner for others preparing, on Fridays.
I keep a spreadsheet of airline requirements (age, height, reach, swimming, grooming, documents) and can share how I organised it.
A trusted circle of Filipino domestic workers in Dubai who meet in Karama every Friday. I can bring a project, a message or a service to them.
Reliable and patient. I can talk through a first swim lesson or a first interview with someone who is scared, because I'm there myself.
My Fridays are free. I can give them to a practice session, a language exchange or a community project.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a cabin crew member (or ex-crew) based in Dubai. I'd be glad to run a mock interview for someone preparing, on a Friday or by video call.
catchers.can: Maricel can do a full mock interview with you on a Friday, bring her real answers, and take honest feedback on turning her nanny experience into crew language.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to meet or call on a Friday, or at a time that doesn't depend on weekday daytime?

catchers.hypo: I run a cabin crew training course. We have a weekend, online or scholarship option for people who can't attend weekday evenings or pay the full fee.
catchers.can: Maricel can tell you exactly what she can commit to (Fridays only) and give you an honest picture of how serious she is, so you can judge fit.
catchers.confirm: Is the course actually available on Fridays or weekends, with a fee that is discounted, spread out or waived?

catchers.hypo: I'm an airline recruiter. Are there candidates who can't make weekday open days but can do an online or weekend application?
catchers.can: Maricel can apply through whatever channel you tell her and share her preparation (CV, requirements checklist, practice) beforehand.
catchers.confirm: Do you have a recruitment route that does not require attending a weekday open day in person?

catchers.hypo: I teach adults to swim and I'm good with people who are afraid of deep water. Do you know anyone who needs that?
catchers.can: Maricel is learning and still panics when her feet leave the floor. Her current coach (Faisal) is patient, and she could use an extra session or a trusted floating technique before a crew assessment.
catchers.confirm: Do you coach adult beginners who are nervous in water, with a session available on Fridays?

catchers.hypo: I'm a teacher or school administrator in Dubai. I know nannies who want to become teachers, and I'd like to help them find a route.
catchers.can: Through her friend Joy, a nanny who wants to become a teacher, Maricel can pass on a route or a contact, with Joy's agreement.
catchers.confirm: Are you offering a concrete step into teaching (training, volunteering or an assistant role) for someone currently working as a nanny?

catchers.hypo: I'm starting a support group or skills workshop for domestic workers in Dubai (interviews, English, finance, swimming). Could your network join?
catchers.can: Maricel can pass the invitation to the Filipino domestic worker group that meets in Karama on Fridays and help get people to a Friday session.
catchers.confirm: Does your event run on a Friday, and is it free or low-cost for domestic workers?

catchers.hypo: My family in Cebu is looking for a reliable, honest person in Dubai to take care of a child or to advise on working abroad.
catchers.can: Maricel can talk about what life as a nanny in Dubai is really like, and may know a friend in her network looking for work.
catchers.confirm: Is this about getting advice or an introduction, rather than hiring Maricel away from her current family?

catchers.hypo: I'm a parent in Dubai looking for a nanny or babysitter. Do you know someone good with school-age children?
catchers.can: Maricel can't take the job herself, but she can refer someone from her Filipino domestic worker friends she trusts.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for a nanny for school-age children rather than a live-in post for Maricel?

forbids.text: I can't attend anything on weekdays; Friday is my only day off.
I can't pay course fees or deposits upfront.
I'll be in Cebu from 18 December for my sister's wedding.
I won't share details of the family I work for, including their private life.
I won't take risks with my current job or with the children's care for a faster route to something else.

projects.name: Cabin crew application
projects.text: Prepare and apply for cabin crew before I turn 30 next year. This covers interview practice, grooming, reach test, swimming ability and the application route, all fitted around Fridays-only availability.
roles_needed: Cabin crew or ex-crew mock interviewer and mentor
Training provider with a Friday, weekend, online or scholarship option
Recruiter who can explain non-weekday application routes
Adult swim coach for nervous beginners
Practice partners for Friday mock interviews

policy.t1: Her daily routine, swimming lessons, friends, her cabin crew goal and timeline, her Friday-only availability, and that she can't afford the academy fees.
policy.t2: Her fear of failing, her worry about age after 30, and her family money obligations.
policy.never: Her savings, her employer's private life, and any identifying details of the family she works for.
